pages.title: HARVEST
pages.text:
STORE

PACKAGE

Before you begin, it is important to understand the three words that you will hear frequently in this module:

Harvesting means picking fruit or vegetables at the right time, without damaging them.

Storing means keeping produce in good conditions so that it stays fresh longer.

Packaging means washing, sorting, and wrapping produce so that it can be easily sold, transported, or stored.

pages.title: STEP 1: HARVEST AT THE RIGHT TIME AND USING
pages.text: THE RIGHT TECHNIQUES
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour ÉTAPE 1 : RÉCOLTER AU BON MOMENT ET AVEC

pages.title: COLOR
pages.text:
FIRMNESS

SMELL / TASTE

You should harvest fruit and vegetables when they are ripe.

To do this, you need to look at several things:

The color: it changes as the produce ripens.

The firmness: by touching it, you can feel whether the fruit is still hard or starting to soften.

The smell and sometimes the taste: ripe fruit often smells good and tastes good if you can taste it.

pages.title: TOO SOON
pages.text:
If you harvest too early, the product is still hard and has no taste.

If you harvest too late, it may be damaged and difficult to sell.

TOO LATE

pages.title: EARLY MORNING
pages.text:
Always harvest early in the morning or late in the day when it is cooler.

Cool temperatures help preserve crops better.

Use your hands or clean, sharp tools such as pruning shears or scissors.

Cut or detach the vegetables carefully.

Place them gently in baskets or buckets, without throwing them.

Avoid knocking or crushing them.

The more carefully you harvest, the longer your produce will keep.

pages.title: Wash your vegetables with clean, drinkable water.
pages.text:
Do not use water from canals or backwaters: it may be dirty and transmit diseases.

Rub your vegetables gently to clean them thoroughly without damaging them.

If you sell or store products, remember to disinfect them.

For example, use a few drops of food-grade bleach in a bucket of clean water.

Then rinse with clean, drinkable water.

pages.title: To prevent vegetables from coming into contact with dirty surfaces, set up a cleaning station.
pages.text:
Use basins or buckets to separate dirty water from clean water.

Prepare a clean table to place the washed vegetables on.

Prepare a suitable storage area :

Choose a cool, shaded location.

Sweep and wash the area before use.

Protect the area from insects, animals, and rodents.

Store your produce properly:

Only store healthy vegetables: no damaged, dirty, or rotten produce.

Do not place them directly on the floor: use baskets or shelves.

Cover them with a damp cloth to keep them fresh.

Do not pile them too high to avoid heat and crushing.

Write on a label: the harvest date, the name of the product, the place or field of origin. This allows you to better

manage your stock and reassure your buyers.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour ATE

pages.title: REMOVE DAMAGED PRODUCTS
pages.text:
VENTILATE

Every day:

Check your food: immediately remove any items that are starting to spoil to prevent them from contaminating

others.

Ventilate regularly: open doors or windows for a few hours each day to prevent mold growth.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour RETIRER PRODUITS ABÎMÉS

pages.title: STEP 4: TRANSPORT WITHOUT DAMAGE
pages.text: STEP 4: TRANSPORT WITHOUT DAMAGE
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour ÉTAPE 4 : TRANSPORTER SANS DÉGÂTS

pages.text:
👍

When your vegetables leave the field, they must be transported with care.

Improper transportation can ruin your entire harvest.

Avoid plastic bags; instead, use baskets, tubs, or open-sided crates to prevent heat buildup and suffocation.

Do not pack the vegetables too tightly so they can breathe and are not crushed. Place the most fragile items

on top.

Transport early in the morning or late in the day to avoid the heat.

Transport quickly: the shorter the transport time, the better.
